title: Full RFID and NFC Product Catalog: 191 SKU variants
summary: The full Proud Tek catalog spans 191 SKU variants across cards, tags, labels, readers, keyfobs and wristbands. Filter by chip family or environment to surface the SKUs that match your reader, frequency and deployment constraints. Each SKU links to the product page with the full chip specification, compatibility notes and inquiry path.
heroPoints: 191 SKUs across HF/NFC and UHF chip families with full specification on every product page.
Filter by chip (NTAG, MIFARE, ICODE, EM, Impinj, Alien, UCODE) and environment (anti-metal, high-temp, outdoor, embed, tamper, sensor).
Every SKU is in stock or sourceable in 5–7 working days for sampling.

sections.title: How to use the catalog
sections.intro: The catalog is organized by product family first, then by chip family within each family. The fastest path depends on what is already locked in your project.
bullets: If chip family is locked → pick the family hub directly (e.g. /products/rfid-cards/) and filter by chip.
If reader is locked → start with /compatibility/ for chip-family validation, then jump into the catalog.
If application is locked → start with /industries/ for SKU recommendations.
If still shortlisting → start with /compare/ to narrow one decision at a time.
If a sample is ready to brief → /contact/ with chip, housing and quantity in the first email.

sections.title: What to expect on every product page
sections.intro: Each SKU page is built around the technical decisions buyers actually need to make. We do not bury the chip family three clicks down or hide the operating frequency under marketing copy.
bullets: Chip family, frequency band, memory layout and read range listed up top.
Anti-metal, IP rating, temperature range and tamper behaviour where applicable.
Available housing variants, colors and printing options.
Standard MOQ, sample turnaround and reorder lead time.
Encoding options (UID lock, NDEF, EPC) and per-piece UID export.
Compliance documentation included on every shipment.

sections.title: Single-vendor procurement across product families
sections.intro: Many Proud Tek customers run programs that span more than one product family. For example, hotel groups deploy key cards, mini wristbands and asset tags from a single PO. The same factories produce all six families, so consolidated documentation and aligned MOQ economics are realistic.
bullets: Hotels: key cards + room wristbands + minibar NFC stickers + housekeeping asset tags.
Industrial laundry: PPS tags + textile UHF tags + cart asset tags + handheld readers.
Retail: source-tag UHF inlays + hangtag labels + handheld readers + EAS-converted tags.
Events: silicone wristbands + paper wristbands + access control keyfobs + handheld readers.
Healthcare: patient wristbands + asset tags + medication labels + compatible HF readers.

resourceCards.title: Shortlisting paths
resourceCards.description: If you are not sure which SKU to choose, these paths let you narrow the decision before sampling.

faq.question: Are all 191 SKUs available for sampling?
faq.answer: Yes: every SKU listed is either in stock or sourceable in 5–7 working days. SKUs with custom housing, anti-metal lamination or bespoke printing add 3–5 days for the first sample.

faq.question: Do you have an order minimum across the whole catalog?
faq.answer: MOQ is per SKU, not per order. Standard MOQ is 500 pieces for cards, 1,000 pieces for tags and labels, 100 pieces for keyfobs and wristbands. Mixed-SKU orders that hit each MOQ individually are the most economical.

faq.question: Can I get prices listed publicly on the site?
faq.answer: No. Pricing depends on chip family, quantity, housing, printing and encoding options. Send a brief through /contact/ and we will return a transparent BOM-level quote within one working day.

faq.question: What if my SKU is not in the catalog?
faq.answer: Most B2B RFID/NFC requirements fit one of the 191 SKUs with minor housing, printing or chip-family variations. If your spec is genuinely outside the catalog (custom antenna geometry, sensor integration, extreme-environment housing) we still take the brief. We will tell you up front whether it fits our manufacturing capability.
